orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Manoj Kumar Tiwari,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Pankaj Purohit
orders.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Bail Application (IA No.2/2023)
In
Criminal Appeal No.177 of 2023
Jagveer Singh ….....Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ….….Respondent
Present:-
Mr. V.B.S. Negi, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. H.S. 
Rawal and Mr Amit Kapri, learned counsel(s) for the 
appellant.
Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate General along with 
Mr. Sidhartha Sah, learned counsel for the informant.
ORDER
Coram: Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
 Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
Appellant/applicant-Jagveer Singh is under 
incarceration on his conviction vide judgment and order 
dated 16.03.2023, passed by learned 2nd Additional 
Sessions Judge, Rudrapur, U.S. Nagar in Sessions Trial 
No.87 of 2018, whereby he has been convicted and 
sentenced as under:-
S.
No.
Conviction Sentence Fine Sentence in-lieu of fine
1. 147 IPC 01 year R.I. - -
2. 148 IPC 02 years’ R.I. Rs.500/- One month 
additional 
imprisonment
3. 307 r/w 
149 IPC
07 years’ R.I. Rs.2,000/- Three months’ 
additional 
imprisonment
4. 302 r/w 
149 IPC
Life 
Imprisonment
Rs.5,000/- Six months’ additional 
imprisonment
All the sentences were directed to run concurrently.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties. 2
3. Since the objection to the bail application has
already been filed by the State, the appellant would press 
the bail application today.
4. The prosecution was set in motion when a 
written complaint dated 07.01.2018 was filed by 
informant-Angrej Singh in P.S. Sitarganj stating therein 
that his father was murdered on 17.07.2015, in which he 
was informant; in the said case, the cross examination 
(Jirah) was left to be made; the accused persons of that 
incident were pressurizing upon him for compromise. 
Due to this enmity on 07.01.2018 at about 01:15 p.m., 
when his cousins-Daljeet Singh, Rajwinder Singh, S/o 
Gurmukh Singh and Kuldeep Singh, S/o Surjeet Singh 
and relatives of the informant; Harbans Singh, S/o 
Jageer Singh were participating in Nagar Kirtan, when 
they reached near Old Mandi Gate, Harjeet Singh @ Kala, 
S/o Manveer Singh, Prabhjot Singh @ Jota, S/o Sarjeet 
Singh, Gurpej Singh, S/o Jageer Singh, Baljeet Singh @ 
Jeeta S/o Manveer Singh, Tarsem Singh S/o Mukhtyar 
Singh, Jajpal Singh S/o Nirvair Singh, R/O Village 
Dehda, P.S. Sitarganj, District Udham Singh Nagar 
attacked the informant and his companions-Daljeet 
Singh, Rajwinder Singh, Kuldeep Singh and Harbans 
Singh with sharp-edged weapons, Lathi, Danda and 
Tamancha with common intention to kill them. In the 
said incident, co-accused-Harjeet Singh @ Kala inflicted 
a fatal blow on the neck of Daljeet Singh with sword and 
stabbed sword in the stomach of Harbans Singh; 
co-accused-Tarsem Singh inflicted on the head of 
Rajwinder Singh with Gandasa which landed at the right 
side of Rajwinder’ face and right hand. Co-accused￾Prabhjot Singh shot a fire from Tamancha (country made  3
pistol) and other above mentioned accused chased them 
with the weapons in their hands with the intention to kill 
them; in between Rajwinder Singh and Kuldeep Singh 
saving their lives fled from the spot. In this incident, 
Daljeet Singh and Harbans Singh died on the spot; 
injured-Rajwinder Singh was taken to Krishna Hospital, 
Haldwani by the informant-Angrej Singh and other 
people. 
5. After investigation, the charge-sheet was 
submitted and on conclusion of trial, the 
appellant/applicant-Jagveer Singh was convicted as 
stated above along with other co-accused. 
6. Learned Senior Advocate appearing for the 
appellant submits that appellant/applicant is not named 
in the FIR and no charge-sheet was filed against him. 
According to learned Senior Advocate, the name of the 
appellant/applicant came in evidence on examination of 
a CCTV footage of the incident by the prosecution 
witnesses and he was summoned to face the trial by 
invoking the provisions of Section 319 of the Cr.P.C.
7. It is vehemently argued by learned Senior 
Advocate appearing for the appellant/applicant that from 
CCTV footage only the presence of appellant/applicant is
seen on the spot and no overt action could be seen and 
attributed to him during the incident. He further submits 
that though the role of exhortation was given to the 
appellant/applicant, but he has been convicted by 
learned trial court under Sections 302/307 IPC with the 
aid of Section 149 IPC. He also submits that since no role 
has been assigned to the appellant/applicant and no 
overt action has been attributed to him; he cannot be 
convicted with the aid of Section 149 IPC. 4
8. In order to buttress his argument, learned 
Senior Advocate appearing for the appellant/applicant 
relied upon the judgment of Hon’ble Apex Court in the 
case of Daya Kishan vs. State of Haryana; reported in 
(2010) 5 SCC 81 and submits that in order to convict a 
person with the aid of Section 149 IPC some overt action 
is needed. 
9. Per contra, learned Deputy Advocate General 
for the State submits that though the 
appellant/applicant was put to trial after invoking the 
provisions of Section 319 of the Cr.P.C. yet that cannot 
be a sole ground to release the appellant/applicant on 
bail. He vehemently argued that the presence of 
appellant/applicant-Jagveer Singh is evident from the 
CCTV footage wherein he was clearly seen and identified 
by the witnesses and from CCTV footage, he is seen in 
scuffle with Daljeet Singh and Rajwinder Singh (page 98 
of the paper book 13.17 min 29 sec.) that is sufficient to 
attract Section 149 IPC for convicting the 
appellant/applicant. He further relied upon the para of 
22 of the judgment of Hon’ble Apex Court in the case of 
Prabhu Dayal vs. State of Rajasthan; reported in 
(2018) 8 SCC 127 and submits that a member of 
unlawful assembly can be prosecuted for the criminal act
of the unlawful assembly and it need not to be proved 
that he had committed overt act. 
10. Apart from that, it is argued that by learned 
State Counsel that this is a double murder case and 
moreover, the murdered persons are the witnesses in the 
murder trial of father of informant-Angrej Singh (PW1). 
Co-accused Harjeet Singh @ Kala and Prabhjot Singh @ 
Jota are the accused in the murder trial of father of  5
informant-Angrej Singh. He also argued that the murder 
was committed by the appellant/applicant with other 
co-accused in the midst of crowd in Nagar Kirtan and in 
broad daylight at about 01:15 p.m.
11. Learned counsel appearing for the informant 
also addressed the Court and vehemently opposed the 
bail application on the same ground as argued by 
learned Deputy Advocate General for the State.
12. Having considered the rival submissions of 
learned counsel for the parties and having gone through 
the paper book of the appeal, since the gruesome murder 
was committed by a group of people in unlawful 
assembly of which the appellant/applicant was also a 
member, he is not entitled to be released on bail. 
Accordingly, bail application is hereby rejected. 
13. List in due course.
14. It is made clear that the observations made 
hereinabove are only for the purpose of deciding the 
present bail application and will not affect the final 
merits of the case.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari,J.)
 06.08.2024
AK

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
18.11.2025 IA No.6 of 2025 (Short Term Bail Application)
In
CRLA 177 of 2023
Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior 
Counsel assisted by Mr. Shubhang Dobhal, 
learned counsel for the appellant/applicant.
2. Mr. J. S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State of Uttarakhand. 
3. The appellant is seeking short term bail 
for a period of 180 days in ST No.87 of 2018 
wherein the appellant/applicant came to be 
convicted for the offences punishable, among 
other offences, under Sections 302 and 307 
IPC, registered at P.S. Sitarganj, District 
Udham Singh Nagar.
4. This Court has been consistently 
disposing of such applications by the following 
order:-
“Learned Deputy Advocate General would 
take this Court through Rule 504 of the 
Uttarakhand Jail Manual (Rules), 2023, which 
deals with ‘Parole & Furlough’. Rule 504(ii) deals 
with objectives of releasing a prisoner on parole 
and furlough, and the same are detailed in 
clauses (a) to (h). Rule 504(ii)(c) enables the 
authorities to release the prisoner on parole or 
furlough to maintain and develop his self￾confidence. 
Learned Deputy Advocate General would 
further take this Court through Rule 512 of the 
Uttarakhand Jail Manual Rules, 2023 to contend 
that such applications are to be placed before the 
competent Authority, i.e. I.G. (Prisons), and the 
competent Authority is required to consider the 
release of the convict in terms of the provisions 
of Rule 512 of the Uttarakhand Jail Manual Rules, 
2023.
In that view, the Short Term Bail 
Application is disposed of by granting liberty to 
the applicant / appellant to submit an Application  to the competent Authority / I.G. (Prisons), and 
if such an Application for release on parole is 
preferred by the applicant / convict, the same 
shall be considered and disposed of by the 
competent Authority within one week.
In the event such application is rejected, it 
is open to the applicant/ appellant to seek 
remedy in accordance with law. 
Registry to forward the copy of this order 
to the competent authority by Email and with a 
copy to the learned Deputy Advocate General. 
In view of the short window of time 
available, we request the learned Deputy 
Advocate General to communicate the orders.”
5. Learned counsel for the appellant would 
place reliance on an order passed by a Co￾ordinate Bench, of which one of us was a 
member, in Criminal Appeal No.210 of 2019,
wherein the Co-ordinate Bench took note of 
the age and adverted to the medical condition 
of appellant in paragraph no.8 and has 
concluded in paragraph no.9 as under:
“8. In fact, during the course of hearing, 
letter addressed to Jail Superintendant by the 
Senior Resident, Cardiology Department, AIIMS 
Rishikesh, has also been placed for the perusal of 
the Court. Let it be taken on record. It records as 
follows:-
“This is regarding Patient Dalbeer 
Singh, 75/M, UHID: 20250044893, on 
11.04.2024, admitted in cardiology unit 2, 
on 11.04.2024, under Dr Barun Kumar, 
prisoner at CENTRAL JAIL, SITARGANJ, 
UTTARAKHAND, with a diagnosis of 
CAD/CCS III/RECURRENT SYNCOPE (2 
Degree AV BLOCK)/NSR/LVEF 60%. The 
patient needs LBB pacemaker (DUAL 
CHAMBER PERMANENT 3 PACEMAKER- MRI 
COMPATIBLE). Its estimated cost is 
approximately 2.5 Lakh Rupees. I 
sincerely request you to look into the 
matter and arrange for finances of the 
same.”
9. The health condition, which is 
deteriorating of the appellant-Dalveer Singh, is a 
circumstance, which commands this Court to 
release the appellant-Dalveer Singh on interim 
bail for a period of 6 months.” 6. Based on the said finding bail application 
of the 80 years old was considered to enable 
him to have treatment in a hospital of his 
choice and in the company of his family 
memebers.
7. In the instant case, learned Deputy 
Advocate General would submit that the 
appellant has been admitted to AIIMS, 
Rishikesh and he is being treated both at 
AIIMS Rishikesh and Sushila Tiwari Hospital, 
Haldwani for a coronary condition. 
8. In that view, we are of the opinion that 
considering the age of the appellant i.e. 65 
years old, we deem it appropriate to direct the 
Jail Authority concerned to permit any one 
family member to remain with the appellant in 
the hospital and also permit the appellant to 
have home cooked food and other articles of 
comfort may also be provided with the 
permission of the Jail Authority.
9. IA No.6 of 2025 stands ordered 
accordingly. Notwithstanding the disposal, we 
grant liberty to the appellant to make 
appropriate application under Rule 504 of the 
Uttarakhand Jail Manual (Rules), 2023, as 
noted supra, and seek for parole.
10. If such an application is made, the same 
shall be considered and disposed of by the 
competent authority within two weeks.
11. List this case in due course.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.) 
 18.11.2025 18.11.2025
KK/SS
